summary: The root cause is right and the 3-line keep-alive is enough. It changes only prepare's E race (_eae_class at T=256 cold), so kernel_fn's timed path and all routes and picks are byte-identical. Expected headline is flat; the run is a correctness/stability check, not a perf lead.
justification: The root cause checks out. _rt_graph (submission.py:4199) returns only (graph, out) and drops fn. torch.cuda.CUDAGraph keeps no reference to tensors allocated outside the capture. So once _rt_graph returns, the only reference to h3/y3/l3 (the lambda's default args) dies. The next arm iteration rebinds h3/y3/l3, which frees the previous set back to the caching allocator, while iso[('c', a)] still writes to those addresses during _rt_time's warm and timed replays. That is a use-after-free that depends on allocator layout, which matches the node evidence (fails 5/5 with the sglang baseline in process, passes once kept alive). On the last arm the tensors also outlive the loop only by accident of scoping. The fix appends (h3, y3, l3) to keep before capture and deletes keep only after _rt_time and the sync. Is it sufficient? Every other buffer the E-phase graphs touch is alive across replay. (a) graphs[a] = _rt_graph(lambda: kernel_fn(data, state)) allocates its intermediates inside the capture, so they live in the graph's private pool, which the graph keeps. Its inputs are data (alive for the whole draw and deleted only after graphs) and persistent state buffers. outs[a] is kept. (b) The iso graph's other operands are data['hidden_states'] and cold (locals alive through _rt_time) plus ea[...] persistent buffers (w13r/w2r/w13e*/w2e*, gs13/gs2, ws13x/ws2x, tk13x/tk2x, errx). The w13e*/w2e* pops in _eae_run happen after every _eae_class has returned and its graphs are deleted. (c) _eae_hy and the post-pick state-copy check run eagerly, with no graphs. (d) _rt_time's empty baseline graph has no operands. (e) Per the triage note, _wh_time's out and _wh_replay's outs stay referenced through _rt_time. kind 't1' and 'hot' never build iso graphs (cold is None). Weakest link: the cold tensor is a slice of _hm_align's output. If that is a view into a persistent hm buffer that kernel_fn's own T=256 replay rewrites, the iso graph's routing could change between replays. That affects only the values in the print-only crat, not memory safety or picks.
confounders: engine-a-a4b-a5b-encodings-race (bbd1661f) introduced _eae_class and the iso cold graphs. This fix only repairs its prepare-time race and does not change what that race picks: crat is print-only, and picks come from rat on the kernel_fn graphs.
v4x256 / v4x256c (T=256 hybrid cold half on v4cxs) is what makes _eae_base accept kind 'cold' at T=256 and so reach the buggy branch. Not a confounder for perf, since the timed path is unchanged.
interference: No companions. The diff changes no kernel, route, threshold or pick input: it only extends the lifetime of three prepare-only scratch tensors until after timing. Any headline delta is run-to-run noise. The only thing to read from the run is whether prepare completes and whether [ea-enc] PATH CHOSEN matches master's picks.
freshness: BEST 2.0201 (24f183ff300949f2) on blob c6e41c9a, the same as at mint (moved 0.00% < 1.24% margin), so it is fresh. No CLAIMS line covers this mechanism. It is a bug fix to the landed engine-a-a4b-a5b-encodings-race prepare race, not a perf mechanism, so E(i)-(iii) do not apply. The branch differs from master only by this 5-line submission.py hunk (other stat lines are docs that the branch predates).
open_questions: Is cold (_hm_align(...)[1][6]) a view into a persistent hm buffer that kernel_fn's T=256 replays overwrite? If so, the printed 'cold iso' ratios time a drifting routing. This is harmless to picks but worth knowing before trusting crat.
Optional hardening: have _rt_graph return or hold fn (e.g. attach it to the graph object) so that every future external-buffer capture is kept alive by construction.
